verdict: Microsoft grew 16% to $65.6B as Azure jumped 33% and Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $38.9B — it kept $24.7B as profit, while Xbox got a big one-year lift from the Activision acquisition.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Office 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics — Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud grew 15% and LinkedIn 10%.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure and server products — Azure and other cloud services grew 33%, the fastest-growing large piece.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows, Xbox and search ads — Xbox content and services up 61% on the Activision acquisition, search ads up 18%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Spending on building products, led by AI and cloud — up 13% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling and marketing the product line — up 10% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 14% YoY.

follow100Note: The rows reconcile to the $37.61 kept as profit within $0.01 of rounding; other expense is a $0.43 drag per $100 of revenue.
footerNote: Segments use Microsoft's FY25 reporting structure (three segments).

takeaways.title: Azure is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Azure and other cloud services grew 33%, and Microsoft Cloud overall reached $38.9B — about 59% of all revenue — as AI demand pulled customers onto the platform.

takeaways.title: The cloud is most of Microsoft now
takeaways.text: Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $38.9B, up 22%. The growth story is the data centers — and the cost of revenue rose 23% as Microsoft built them out.

takeaways.title: Xbox got an acquisition lift
takeaways.text: Xbox content and services revenue jumped 61%, but 53 points of that came from the Activision acquisition closing a year earlier — the underlying games business grew much more slowly.
